title: Canonical queue projection requires deterministic preflight classification

observed: CM-1011 established that canonical queue authority is field-scoped and time-scoped.
The canonical queue snapshot predates later additive continuity records.
Before this slice, no committed validator classified additive records as duplicated, conflicting, or safely promotable without modifying the canonical queue.
The new validator performs no mutation and emits a reason-coded classification report.
inferred: Temporal precedence alone is insufficient for promotion; owner agreement, queue-item existence, non-duplication, non-regression, and a non-empty completed slice are also required.
A newer additive record can still conflict with canonical authority even when its timestamp is valid.
Projection safety improves when promotion eligibility is separated from the act of canonical mutation.
proposed: Run the validator before every canonical queue reconciliation.
Permit canonical promotion only for records classified safely_promotable and preserve duplicated or conflicting records as immutable evidence rather than deleting them.
Extend the validator later with explicit acceptance-criteria and state-transition compatibility rules.
superseded: Treating every post-snapshot additive update as automatically promotable.
Using timestamp comparison as the sole reconciliation rule.
Combining projection analysis and canonical mutation in one irreversible step.
unresolved: The canonical queue still has not been reconciled with all later continuity slices.
The validator does not yet prove exhaustive discovery of every additive queue-update file.
The immutable origins of M-004, M-005, and M-006 remain unlocated.

classification_contract.pending: Reserved for records not yet fully classified by a caller-specific policy.
classification_contract.duplicated: The normalized completed slice is already present in the canonical item.
classification_contract.conflicting: The record violates queue identity, ownership, state, timestamp, or minimum-content constraints.
classification_contract.safely_promotable: The record is newer than the canonical snapshot, owner-consistent, non-duplicative, and contains a completed slice.

privacy_boundary.publication_rule: Retain only repository governance, provenance, and deterministic reconciliation mechanics.

falsification_route: Provide a counterexample where the validator marks a conflicting or duplicate record safely_promotable, or show that a required canonical authority field is omitted from its decision contract.
next_action: Use authenticated all-refs and object traversal to determine whether M-004, M-005, and M-006 have immutable repository provenance; keep them unresolved unless exhaustive evidence supports location or unlocated classification.
